It was accurate at 21:4xZ and stale within the hour: the traffic read taken immediately before this lane's final shift (_inbox/2026-09-17_g150-reasoner-path-build_traffic-before.json) shows plan-review-00027-luk -- this lane's own first canary -- at 100 percent with plan-review-00029-gom already tagged, and the field-name read at 2026-09-17T22:48:55Z shows 00029-gom serving while 00025-ley holds only the tag g126-tenant-isolation with no percent field at all. Disclosed, not smoothed. G-107 (capturing the dimension as a reading) is not built: the provenance ladder's top rung is declared with owner G-107 and the claim that capturing it upgrades the INPUT and does not unlock the determination. Nothing in this lane changes that.

The registry serves one ruleKey. When a second adjudicator is registered for real (not as a fixture), the badge rule is already proven to follow the registry; the risk is a design redraw that hard-codes the badge, which check.mjs now catches.

Web/app.js renders a Reasoning tab; it is not reviewed against the SmartCity visual law in this lane (quiet surfaces, inverted applicability, 12px floor, no bare confidence) -- the drawn artboards ARE that law, and the live tab is a plain render of the same fields.
The pre-contract engagements' repair decision (see leave_behind) and the SF-1 label defect are the two threads a successor should pick up first.

LESSON: 'Every claim traced to commit X' ages silently: the dump must be re-taken after the LAST code commit, or the design is being compared against a tree nobody is shipping (caught here only because a later commit moved the head).

A badge is only checkable if the surface carries the registry it was derived from. A design check cannot verify badge derivation against the design alone; the served JSON had to gain a `registry` field for the comparison to exist.

A 500 with prose and no code cannot be classified by anything reading the surface -- not a probe, not a reviewer. Three of seven demo engagements sat unreadable for exactly that reason until the refusal carried a named code.

An instrument must be run in BOTH directions or it cannot be distinguished from a control that never fires: 8 defects in this lane's own instrument (three false positives, one false negative, one vacuity, one harness non-event, one ordering error, one self-comparison) were invisible by reading it.
DEAD_END: Proving badge derivation from the artboard alone -- the drawing can only be compared to something the product emitted; abandoned in favour of the served registry in the same response.

Repairing the three pre-contract engagements with a migration inside this lane -- the repair is a semantic decision about what those engagements should say, so it was deferred with its refusal codes named rather than guessed.
